# Computer Science > Machine Learning

[Submitted on 31 Aug 2026]

# Title: Tensor Methods for Language Models: From Token Representation to Training, Adaptation, Inference, Compression, and Interpretability

Authors: Matvei Tarasov , Salman Ahmadi-Asl , Andre L. F. de Almeida , Andrzej Cichocki

View a PDF of the paper titled Tensor Methods for Language Models: From Token Representation to Training, Adaptation, Inference, Compression, and Interpretability, by Matvei Tarasov and 3 other authors

View PDF HTML (experimental)

> Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are built from structured high-dimensional objects such as token representations, weights, adaptation updates, caches, and activations, whose multilinear structure is underexploited by the conventional matrix-centric view. Tensor decompositions and tensor networks provide a principled algebraic language for this structure, yet the literature often treats them as isolated compression mechanisms. This survey organizes tensor methods for LLMs through two complementary views: a seven-stage lifecycle taxonomy covering tokenization, embeddings, pre-training, adaptation, compression, inference, and interpretability, and a component view covering embeddings, attention, and feed-forward networks. We provide unified notation and theoretical foundations, analyze tensorization strategies for individual Transformer components, and compare methods at each lifecycle stage while making differences in evaluation protocols and model scales explicit. We further connect tensor methods to neighboring efficiency techniques and probabilistic tensor networks. Finally, we synthesize open challenges and introduce gap, a metric for the compression-realization gap between theoretical memory reduction and measured system-level speedup. By treating tensorization as a common structural principle, the survey provides a structured entry point to tensorized language models and clarifies when parameter savings can plausibly translate into memory efficiency, computational efficiency, or interpretability. The GitHub page dedicated to this paper is accessible at this https URL.

summaryZh: 本文系统性地综述了张量方法在大型语言模型（LLM）全生命周期中的应用，涵盖了从分词、嵌入、预训练到推理、压缩及可解释性的七个阶段。作者通过统一的代数视角，分析了张量分解与张量网络如何优化Transformer组件，并提出了衡量压缩与系统级加速之间差距的指标“ρ gap”。该研究不仅为模型参数压缩提供了理论支撑，还为提升计算效率和模型可解释性提供了结构化的方法论参考。

glossary.explanationZh: 张量分解，用于将高维权重矩阵分解为低秩张量以减少参数量。
张量网络，一种用于表示和处理高维数据的数学框架。
衡量理论内存减少与实际系统级加速之间差距的指标。
多线性结构，指模型权重和激活值中蕴含的非矩阵化高维关联。
